Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every unexplained variance above tolerance, every reconciling item unresolved at approval and every variance that later drives an amended return is logged with the state, the dollar amount, the tax effect and the resolution date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Controller signs the completed reconciliation and every correction that changes either the filed statutory premium or the taxed premium

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All 51 jurisdiction reconciliations for the tax year — Schedule T direct written premium against taxed premium per filed return, by writing company

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Unexplained variance above the lower of $100,000 or 1% of a state's direct written premium is a fail; any variance that understates taxed premium is a fail regardless of size and triggers an amended return assessment

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is annual and gated on the filed annual statement; the test runs annually after the March filing season and again on any state where an amended annual statement or amended return was lodged

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must be independent of both the tax preparers and the statutory reporting team that produced Schedule T

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual premium tax reconciliation test workpaper (population, Schedule T re-extract, variance re-performance, reconciling item vouching, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under Tax / Premium Tax Reconciliation / <tax year>

Regulator-ready documentation.value: The state-by-state reconciliation grid with the Schedule T tie and the itemised reconciling items, producible to a state premium tax examiner within 10 business days as the standard opening request in a premium tax audit

Regulator response path.value: Tax Director owns premium tax examination correspondence; the Statutory Reporting Manager supplies any annual statement explanation and Regulatory Counsel clears any position on a disputed basis difference

checklist.step: Wait for the annual statement to file, then extract Schedule T as the source of record
actions: Confirm the annual statement for the tax year has been filed with the NAIC and the domiciliary regulator before the reconciliation starts — reconciling to a draft statement wastes the cycle.
Export Schedule T showing direct premiums written by state and territory, by writing company and NAIC co-code.
Export the Exhibit of Premiums and Losses (State Page) for each jurisdiction so direct written, direct earned, returned premium and dividends are available by line.
Record the filing date and statement version on the reconciliation cover sheet so the grid names the exact statement it reconciles to.
checklist.done: Schedule T and the State Pages from the as-filed statement are extracted and the grid cover sheet names the statement version and filing date.

checklist.step: Extract the taxed premium actually reported on each filed return
actions: Open each filed premium tax return and read the taxable premium and gross premium lines as filed, not as computed in the workpaper.
Record per state and writing company: gross premium reported, deductions claimed, taxable premium, tax and retaliatory excess.
Where a state's return reports on a collected or received basis rather than written, tag the row with that basis so it is not compared like for like.
Load the extract into the reconciliation grid alongside the Schedule T figures.
checklist.done: the grid holds gross premium, deductions and taxable premium as actually filed for every state and writing company, each tagged with its reporting basis.

checklist.step: Build the state-by-state reconciliation grid
actions: Lay out one row per jurisdiction per writing company with columns for Schedule T direct written premium, return gross premium, reconciling items and the residual variance.
Compute the residual variance in dollars and as a percentage of Schedule T premium for each row.
Add subtotal rows by writing company and a grand total row that ties to the Schedule T grand total.
Apply conditional flags on any row exceeding the lower of $100,000 or 1% so the investigation list is visible on the first screen.
checklist.done: the grid holds one row per state and company with a computed variance, flags above tolerance and a grand total tying to Schedule T.

checklist.step: Document the basis differences between written, earned and collected premium
actions: Identify the jurisdictions that tax premium on a collected or received basis rather than the written basis Schedule T reports.
For each of those states quantify the bridging item from written premium to collected premium using the receivables movement from the billing system for that state.
Ask Billing Operations for the state-level cash-received report and agree the bridging figure to it in writing.
Record the basis and the bridging amount on the grid row with its source report name and date.
checklist.done: every collected-basis state carries a quantified, source-agreed bridge from Schedule T written premium to the premium taxed.

checklist.step: Quantify the deduction reconciling items to the State Pages
actions: For each state, agree returned premium and policyholder dividends claimed on the return to the State Page lines for that jurisdiction.
Agree the exempt government business deduction to the underwriting records identifying federal and state entity policies in that state.
Agree the annuity consideration exclusion to the life company's Schedule T annuity line rather than to a manual list.
Any deduction that cannot be agreed to the statement or an underwriting source stays as an unexplained variance until it can.
checklist.done: every deduction claimed on a return is agreed to a State Page line or an underwriting source, or remains flagged as unexplained.

checklist.step: Isolate assumed, ceded and non-taxable premium flows
actions: Confirm assumed reinsurance premium is excluded from both the Schedule T direct column and the return's taxable base — assumed business is generally not premium-taxed at the assuming company.
Confirm ceded premium was not netted anywhere in the taxable base, since premium tax is levied on direct written premium gross of reinsurance.
Provide the state-level assumed and ceded figures from the reinsurance system so the tax team can prove the exclusion rather than assert it.
Sign the assumed/ceded confirmation sheet and attach it to the grid.
checklist.done: a signed confirmation shows assumed and ceded premium by state and proves neither entered or netted against the taxable base.

checklist.step: Test the fees and charges included in or excluded from the base
actions: Extract policy fees, membership fees, installment and service charges by state from the billing system for the tax year.
Compare each state's treatment on the return to that state's statute — Alabama includes policy and membership fees in gross premium, other states exclude service charges.
Quantify the dollar effect of any state where the treatment on the return differs from the statute and route it to the Tax Manager as a correction candidate.
Record the fee amounts and the treatment decision on the grid row so the position is reconstructible.
checklist.done: fee and charge amounts by state are extracted, compared to statute and quantified, with any misalignment routed for correction.

checklist.step: Reconcile the reported premium back to the general ledger
actions: Extract direct written premium by state and writing company from the GL premium subledger for the tax year.
Compare the GL total to the Schedule T total and explain the difference — statutory-to-GAAP presentation, late entries and reclassifications are the usual causes.
Confirm no state-level premium was reclassified between jurisdictions after the statement was filed without a matching amended statement.
Sign the GL-to-Schedule T tie and attach it to the reconciliation grid.
checklist.done: a signed tie exists between the GL premium subledger, Schedule T and the reconciliation grid, with every difference explained.

checklist.step: Investigate and clear every variance above tolerance
actions: Take the flagged rows and assign each to a named investigator with a due date ahead of the March filing gate.

Require each investigation to end in one of four outcomes: a quantified reconciling item with a source, a correction to the return, a correction to the statutory statement, or an accepted immaterial residual with the Controller's agreement.
Reject 'timing' or 'rounding' as an explanation unless it is quantified and sourced.
Track the flagged rows to zero open items on a daily basis during the filing window.
checklist.done: no row above tolerance remains open at the filing gate; each has a sourced item, a correction, or a Controller-agreed residual.

checklist.step: Feed corrections back into the returns before they are filed
actions: Where the reconciliation shows the taxable base was misstated, update the locked computation tab through the formal change route and record the reason.
Recompute the tax, retaliatory excess and balance due for that state and re-populate the return form from the corrected figures.
Notify the filing team and Treasury of any change to the remittance amount before the payment is released.
Record on the grid row that the correction reached the return, with the new balance due and the date.
checklist.done: every correction identified by the reconciliation is reflected in the locked computation and in the return before submission.

checklist.step: Raise amended returns where a filed return is already wrong
actions: For prior-year returns where the reconciliation reveals understated taxable premium, decide whether to amend or to make a voluntary disclosure and record the reasoning.
Compute the additional tax, penalty and interest at that state's rates from the original due date and get the Controller's approval to pay.
Have Regulatory Counsel clear any covering explanation before the amended return is submitted.
Track the amended return through to state acknowledgement and record the outcome on the grid.
checklist.done: every understatement has an approved amend-or-disclose decision, a computed additional liability and a tracked submission.

checklist.step: Re-run the reconciliation when the annual statement is amended
actions: Notify the Tax Manager within one business day whenever an amended annual statement changes Schedule T or a State Page.
Re-export the changed schedules and mark the reconciliation cover sheet with the new statement version.
Re-run the affected state rows and quantify the tax effect of the restated premium.
Where the restatement increases taxed premium, hand the affected states to the Tax Director for the amended-return decision.
checklist.done: any amended annual statement triggers a re-run of the affected rows within the same reporting cycle, with the tax effect quantified.

checklist.step: Obtain Controller approval on the completed reconciliation
actions: Review the grand total tie to Schedule T, the flagged-row disposition list and the residual unexplained total before signing.
Challenge any accepted residual and confirm each is genuinely below the tolerance rather than an aggregation of items just under it.
Sign and date the reconciliation approval page naming the tax year, the statement version and the total taxed premium by writing company.
Release the approval as the gate that allows the returns to be filed.
checklist.done: a signed, dated approval page exists naming the statement version and total taxed premium, and the filing gate is released.

checklist.step: Report the reconciliation result into the tax and statutory close packs
actions: Add the reconciliation summary — total Schedule T premium, total taxed premium, total reconciling items and residual — to the annual tax close pack.
Report any state where the residual approached tolerance as a watch item into the following year's reconciliation plan.
Circulate the summary to the Statutory Reporting Manager and the Chief Financial Officer with the filing gate status.
Record the reporting date on the reconciliation cover sheet.
checklist.done: the reconciliation summary is in the close pack, circulated to Finance leadership, with watch items carried into next year's plan.

checklist.step: Archive the reconciliation pack for the retention period
actions: Upload the grid, the Schedule T and State Page exports, the return extracts, the reconciling item support, the GL tie and the Controller approval.
Apply the 7-year retention label from the return filing date and index by tax year, jurisdiction, writing company and statement version.
Cross-link the pack to the locked computation and the filed returns so a premium tax examiner can be walked from statement to return in one sitting.
Grant read access to the Internal Auditor and the external auditor and write-lock the folder.
checklist.done: the reconciliation pack is archived, labelled for 7-year retention, indexed by statement version and linked to the computation and returns.

testing.step: Build the population of jurisdiction reconciliations for the tax year
actions: Pull the approved reconciliation pack and list every jurisdiction and writing company row it contains.
Compare that list to Schedule T so every state with reported direct written premium has a reconciliation row, including territories.
Add any jurisdiction where a return was filed but no reconciliation row exists — that combination is an automatic exception.
Record the population count, the statement version reconciled to and the extract date in the workpaper.
testing.done: the population covers every Schedule T jurisdiction and every filed return, with any gap logged as an exception.

testing.step: Re-extract Schedule T independently and agree the grid's source column
actions: Export Schedule T and the State Pages yourself from the as-filed annual statement rather than using the tax team's copy.
Agree the Schedule T column of the reconciliation grid line by line and confirm the grand total ties to the underwriting and investment exhibit.
Confirm the statement version named on the grid cover sheet is the version actually on file, including any amendment.
Any difference between your extract and the grid's source column is an exception before the reconciliation itself is tested.
testing.done: the grid's Schedule T column agrees line by line to an independently sourced extract of the correct statement version.

testing.step: Draw the sample and document the selection method
actions: Take 100% of the ten jurisdictions with the largest direct written premium and 100% of rows whose residual variance was flagged above tolerance.
Draw 10 further jurisdictions by seeded random selection over the remainder.
Include at least one collected-basis state and one state where a correction or amended return arose from the reconciliation.
Record the seed, the population size and the selection date so the sample can be redrawn identically.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible and covers the largest states, all flagged rows, a collected-basis state and a corrected state.

testing.step: Re-perform the variance calculation on the sample
actions: For each sampled row take Schedule T direct written premium and the gross premium on the filed return and compute the raw variance yourself.
Subtract only the reconciling items that carry a named source and recompute the residual.
Compare your residual to the grid's residual and treat any difference as an exception, including cases where the grid's arithmetic is right but an item is unsourced.
Recompute the residual as a percentage of Schedule T premium and re-apply the tolerance test independently.
testing.done: each sampled row has an independently recomputed variance and residual, with the tolerance test re-applied.

testing.step: Vouch each reconciling item to its underlying source
actions: For each reconciling item on a sampled row, pull the cited source — State Page line, billing cash-received report, underwriting exempt-entity listing, reinsurance confirmation — and agree the amount.
Reject any item described only as timing, rounding or reclassification without a quantified source document.
Confirm the item is directionally correct: an item that increases taxed premium must be supported by the same evidence rigour as one that reduces it.
Log unvouched items as unexplained variance and re-apply the tolerance test with them added back.
testing.done: every sampled reconciling item is vouched to a source document, and unvouched items are added back before re-testing tolerance.

testing.step: Test the collected-basis bridge and the fee treatment
actions: For sampled collected-basis states, rebuild the written-to-collected bridge from the billing system's state-level cash-received report and the premium receivable movement.
Compare your bridge to the grid's and quantify any difference in taxable premium and tax.
Extract policy fees, membership fees and installment charges for the sampled states and re-read the statute's inclusion rule for each.
Quantify the tax effect of any fee treated differently from the statute and log it as an exception with its direction.
testing.done: each sampled collected-basis bridge and fee treatment is independently rebuilt and any difference is quantified in tax dollars.

testing.step: Confirm assumed and ceded premium were correctly excluded
actions: Take the assumed and ceded premium by state from the reinsurance records independently of the tax team's confirmation sheet.
Confirm no assumed premium appears in the Schedule T direct column or in any sampled return's taxable base.
Confirm ceded premium was not netted against direct written premium anywhere in the base, since the tax is levied gross of reinsurance.
Quantify the tax effect of any netting or inclusion found and log it as an exception.
testing.done: assumed and ceded premium are independently confirmed as excluded and un-netted for every sampled state, or the effect is quantified.

testing.step: Test the GL tie and the treatment of post-filing premium movements
actions: Extract direct written premium by state from the GL yourself and agree it to the grid's GL tie sheet.
Test for premium reclassified between states after the statement filing date and confirm each reclassification is matched by either an amended statement or an amended return.
Confirm the reconciliation was re-run for every amended annual statement filed in the year, using the amendment log as the population.
Log any restatement that changed taxed premium without a corresponding return action as an exception.
testing.done: the GL tie is independently agreed and every post-filing premium movement is matched to an amended statement or an amended return.

testing.step: Log exceptions with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a tracker issue for each unexplained variance, unvouched item or missing reconciliation naming the state, company, dollar variance and tax effect.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: basis mismatch untracked, deduction unsupported, fee treatment wrong, assumed or ceded contamination, statement restated late, reclassification unmatched.
Assign an owner and a remediation date, and where taxed premium was understated require the Tax Director to record an amend-or-disclose decision.
Carry every open exception into next year's reconciliation test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has a tracker issue, a root cause, a quantified tax effect, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report the result
actions: Total the unexplained variance across the population and compare it to the lower of $100,000 or 1% per-state threshold and the zero-tolerance understatement rule.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions or ineffective — citing the workpaper references and the total tax effect of the exceptions.
Have the workpaper signed by a reviewer independent of both the tax preparers and the statutory reporting team that produced Schedule T.
Report to the Controller, the Chief Financial Officer and the Audit Committee and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository under the tax year.
testing.done: a signed workpaper stating total unexplained variance, the tax effect, the conclusion and the reporting date exists in the repository.
